entry_state: Chapter9 develops operating-company accounting methods before the later uncertainty discussion. Distinct books preserve treatment differences;the inventory example demonstrates their numerical effect. Revenue,unconditional billing,advances and collection are separate transitions. Applied advances reduce both unused credit and the amount still owed;even a zero-money invoice must atomically consume its credit. The next example examines a sale with a surviving return right.
exit_state: Return rights,warranties,contract modifications and principal-agent status require distinct retained facts even when cash agrees. Refund and recovery balances reconcile to cash across two periods;modified distinct units retain past revenue while integrated performance can require a catch-up. Inventory and PPE retain cost and estimate history. The equipment-preparation case has separated machine cost120,sample cost6 and period expense6;its statement consequences continue on page125.
findings: The return case keeps refund liability and recovery asset gross. Updating twelve expected returns to eight actual returns produces profit16 and cash outflow80 in2025 without recognizing a second sale.

The warranty allocation90/18 follows stated standalone prices and uniform performance facts. Modification cases distinguish remaining-unit allocation9 from the integrated obligation's negative1 catch-up.

The principal/agent cases share cash and profit20 but report revenue120 or20 according to control. The equipment example separates sample resources from calibration resources to avoid capitalizing the same cost twice. No confirmed new defect.
